summary.en: Prevent uninitialized pointer use, track target lifetime, and release owned memory without leaving usable aliases.
summary.bn: মান না দেওয়া পয়েন্টার পড়া এড়াও, টার্গেটের মেয়াদ দেখো আর মেমরি ছাড়ার পর পুরোনো অ্যাড্রেস ব্যবহার কোরো না।

notes: Uninitialized reads and expired-object access remain invalid across the C standards in this course. The examples target C17. Sanitizers are compiler tools rather than language guarantees, so their usefulness complements lifetime reasoning instead of replacing it.

examples.title: Initialize before selecting a target
examples.explanationHtml: The pointer is initialized immediately and only dereferenced after a live target is assigned.

examples.title: Copy a value before a block ends
examples.explanationHtml: The int value is copied while local is alive. No expired pointer is read after leaving the block.

examples.title: Release allocated storage once
examples.explanationHtml: Allocation failure is checked. The value is read before free, then the owner is cleared and not reused.

examples.title: An uninitialized pointer is not a destination
examples.explanationHtml: The result is undefined: p was never assigned a valid target address. Initialize a real int and point to it.

examples.title: An alias still expires after free
examples.explanationHtml: The result is undefined: alias still refers to the object whose lifetime ended. Clearing owner does not revive or clear alias.

practice.title: Copy before scope exit
practice.statementHtml: Read an int -100 to 100. Print Local value: then copy it through a pointer inside a nested block and print the saved scalar outside.
hints: Save the value, not the expired address.

practice.title: Use a caller-owned result slot
practice.statementHtml: Read two ints -100 to 100. Print Two integers (-100 to 100): then their sum written into a main-owned int through a helper.
hints: The result slot remains alive after the helper returns.

practice.title: Own one allocated score
practice.statementHtml: Read an int -100 to 100. Print Owned score: then allocate one int, store twice the input, print it and release it.
hints: Only the malloc result is passed to free.

practice.title: Use temporary aliases before release
practice.statementHtml: Read two ints -100 to 100. Print Two owned values: then allocate two ints, sum them through temporary aliases, print the sum, and free the original allocation once.
hints: Limit borrowed aliases to a block ending before free.

quiz.prompt: What is the initial value of an uninitialized automatic int *p?
quiz.explanation: Automatic pointer objects are not implicitly initialized.

quiz.prompt: Does checking an uninitialized p against NULL initialize it?
options: Only if the branch is skipped
quiz.explanation: The comparison reads the indeterminate pointer instead of assigning a known value.

quiz.prompt: When does an automatic local int cease to exist?
quiz.explanation: Keeping its address cannot extend that lifetime.

quiz.prompt: Does owner=NULL after free(owner) clear another pointer alias?
What should be passed to free for a two-element malloc allocation?
options: A pointer to its second element
The address of the owner variable
quiz.explanation: Interior addresses are not valid allocation owners for free.

quiz.prompt: Can a non-null pointer safely prove its former target is still alive?
What is the result of freeing the same allocation twice?
quiz.explanation: free(NULL) is harmless, but reusing a freed block pointer is not.

quiz.prompt: What value appears after initializing and assigning the pointer?
quiz.explanation: A live score is selected before the dereference.

quiz.prompt: Which value survives after the nested local disappears?
What output is produced before and after releasing the owned int?
quiz.explanation: Only the initialized null owner is inspected after free.

keyPoints.en: An uninitialized automatic pointer has an indeterminate value.
keyPoints.bn: মান না দেওয়া অটোমেটিক পয়েন্টারের মান অনির্দিষ্ট থাকে।

keyPoints.en: A pointer can outlive the object it once selected.
keyPoints.bn: যে ভেরিয়েবলের দিকে পয়েন্টার তাক করেছিল, সেটির মেয়াদ আগেই শেষ হতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: free ends an allocated object lifetime.
keyPoints.bn: free করলে অ্যালোকেট করা মেমরির মেয়াদ শেষ হয়।

keyPoints.en: Nulling one owner does not repair its aliases.
keyPoints.bn: একটি পয়েন্টার NULL করলেই তার কপিগুলো নিরাপদ হয় না।

keyPoints.en: Use owned storage only while its lifetime and range are valid.
keyPoints.bn: মেমরি জীবিত ও সীমার মধ্যে থাকলেই অ্যাড্রেস দিয়ে কাজ করো।

examQuestions.question: Distinguish a wild pointer from a dangling pointer and give a prevention technique for each.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A wild pointer usually means an uninitialized pointer whose indeterminate value is not a usable address. Initialize it to NULL or a live object address before any read. A dangling pointer once selected storage whose lifetime ended, through free or scope exit. Keep borrowing inside the owner lifetime, never return automatic local addresses, and discard aliases before release.

45
Released

Only the initialized null owner is inspected after free.

examQuestions.question: Read two ints -100 to 100. Print Two owned values: then allocate two ints, sum them through temporary aliases, print the sum, and free the original allocation once.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main(void)
{
    int a, b;
    puts("Two owned values:");
    if (scanf("%d %d", &a, &b) != 2 || a < -100 || a > 100 || b < -100 || b > 100) {
        return 1;
    }
    int *owner = malloc(2 * sizeof *owner);
    if (owner == NULL) {
        return 1;
    }
    owner[0] = a;
    owner[1] = b;
    {
        const int *left = owner;
        const int *right = owner + 1;
        printf("%d\n", *left + *right);
    }
    free(owner);
    owner = NULL;
    return 0;
}

Limit borrowed aliases to a block ending before free.
